channel.title: Parallax
channel.description: Same event, different vantage points. Geopolitical news compared across Western, Eastern, Middle Eastern and Russian outlets.

item.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO following a period of leadership transition.
item.description: Nvidia’s board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO on November 24, 2026, following a brief resignation sparked by allegations of espionage and an extramarital affair. The move triggered a 32% to 36% surge in share prices after consultations with U.S. officials regarding national security. Western outlets frame the event as a political scandal involving personal scandal and espionage, while Middle Eastern and Russian sources focus on the influence of Silicon Valley over U.S. government policy.

item.title: Multiple oil tankers are reported to have been damaged or set ablaze in the Strait of Hormoz.
item.description: On November 23, 2026, multiple oil tankers were damaged or set ablaze in the Strait of Hormuz. While all sources confirm the physical damage and the resulting fire, coverage diverges on the cause and the identity of the perpetrators. Middle Eastern outlets frame the incident as a failure of Western security and a response to regional threats, while other reports focus on the specific role of naval mines and American policy in the maritime crisis.

item.title: Oxfam reports that Israeli military actions have caused significant environmental and toxic damage in Gaza.
item.description: A joint report by Oxfam and the Conflict and Environment Observatory reveals that 99% of Gaza's land is contaminated with heavy metals and dioxins following Israeli military actions. While both Western and Russian outlets report on the destruction of sewage systems and groundwater, their framing differs. Western media emphasizes the immediate humanitarian crisis and the creation of a "toxic wasteland," while Russian reports focus on the long-term systemic consequences of specific military tactics in Gaza City and Khan Younis.
